name: ParticleEmitter3D
shortDescription: Display a large number of particles in 3D to create visual effects in a 3D game.
description: 3D particle emitters let you create and display many small particles to simulate visual effects in your game — like fire, explosions, smoke, dust, magic, rain or snow.

The parameters of the object can be configured in multiple different ways to create a specific desired effect. GDevelop will give a set of a pre-configured 3D particle emitters that you should try first.

Particles are emitted along the local Z axis of the emitter: upward by default. Rotate the instance to aim the emission (for instance a rotation of 180° on the X axis emits downward, 90° on the Y axis emits toward X). The size of the instance has no effect: particles are emitted from a single point, or from a disc when the "Emission zone radius" property is set (useful for rain or snow falling over a whole area).
Use these 3D particle emitters in 3D games. For 2D games or particles that appear on a game's 2D user interface, use the 2D particle emitter object instead.

changelog.breaking: - the object rotates the other way around X axis.
- Object properties for position and rotation have been removed. They must be set with the instance editor or the action.

propertyDescriptors.label: Start min speed
propertyDescriptors.description: Initial speed of the particles, in the emission direction (the local Z axis of the emitter).
propertyDescriptors.name: StartSpeedMin

propertyDescriptors.label: Particles move with the emitter
propertyDescriptors.description: When checked, the particles already emitted follow the emitter when it moves or rotates. Leave it unchecked for rain, snow or smoke that must stay where it was emitted while the emitter follows the camera or a character.
propertyDescriptors.name: AreParticlesRelative

propertyDescriptors.label: Spray cone angle
propertyDescriptors.description: Spread of the particles around the emission direction, which is the local Z axis of the emitter (upward by default, rotate the instance to aim it). 0 or more than 180 emits in every direction, unless an emission zone radius is set: then 0 emits straight.
propertyDescriptors.name: SpayConeAngle

propertyDescriptors.label: Emission zone radius
propertyDescriptors.description: Particles are emitted from a disc of this radius, perpendicular to the emission direction. 0 emits from a single point. Use a large radius (like 1000) for rain or snow falling over a whole area.
propertyDescriptors.name: ZoneRadius

propertyDescriptors.label: Blending
propertyDescriptors.description: Additive makes particles glow (fire, magic, energy). Use Normal for rain, snow, smoke or dust. Only applied when the object is created.
propertyDescriptors.name: Blending

propertyDescriptors.label: Gravity top
propertyDescriptors.description: Z+: gravity pulls particles down along the Z axis (the usual choice in 3D games). Y-: gravity pulls particles toward Y+.
propertyDescriptors.name: GravityTop

propertyDescriptors.label: Gravity
propertyDescriptors.description: Acceleration pulling the particles in the direction given by the gravity top. 0 disables gravity.
propertyDescriptors.name: Gravity

propertyDescriptors.label: Delete when emission ends
propertyDescriptors.description: Delete the object once the emission duration is over and every particle disappeared. Uncheck it and set the emission duration to 0 for a continuous effect like fire, rain or snow.
propertyDescriptors.name: ShouldAutodestruct

propertyDescriptors.description: Only used by the scene editor.
propertyDescriptors.name: ParentOrigin

propertyDescriptors.label: Start min length
propertyDescriptors.description: Number of past positions kept to draw the trail, one per frame: the visible length is this number multiplied by the distance traveled by the particle each frame.
propertyDescriptors.name: TrailStartLengthMin

propertyDescriptors.label: Start max length
propertyDescriptors.description: Number of past positions kept to draw the trail, one per frame: the visible length is this number multiplied by the distance traveled by the particle each frame.
propertyDescriptors.name: TrailStartLengthMax

propertyDescriptors.label: Render mode
propertyDescriptors.description: "Image facing the camera" draws each particle as an image. "Image following a trail" stretches the image along the path of each particle (sparks, rain streaks).
propertyDescriptors.name: RenderMode
